issue.description:
docs/plan/plan.md section 7.1 documents delta encoding as an intended
optimization for the turns array on long matches ("for very long matches,
the turns array can use delta encoding -- only recording events that
changed from the previous turn") but this is not implemented: engine/replay.go
has no delta logic (grepped for "delta"/"Delta" in engine/replay.go --
only hit is an unrelated Direction.Delta() helper in engine/types.go).
Every turn in a replay is currently stored in full.

Each turn already only records deltas conceptually (moves, spawns,
deaths, captures, energy_collected, energy_spawned, scores -- see the
example schema in section 7.1) rather than full grid state, so the "delta
encoding" here specifically means: don't re-emit unchanged per-player
score/energy totals every turn if they didn't change since the last turn,
and consider omitting turns array entries for structurally uneventful
turns (dedupeable via the existing gzip pass, but true delta encoding
reduces pre-gzip size and, more importantly, parse/reconstruction time in
web/src/lib/replay-data.ts on load).

Concrete scope: measure current uncompressed/gzipped replay size for a
representative 500-turn 4-player match (section 7.1 estimates
200-500KB / 30-80KB), implement delta encoding for the turns array in
engine/replay.go, update the replay format version, update
web/src/lib/replay-data.ts to reconstruct full per-turn state from deltas,
and confirm the replay viewer (web/src/replay-viewer.ts) still renders
identically. Bump replay schema version and update
web/public/replay-schema-v1.json (or introduce v2) accordingly.

Value: smaller payload = faster replay-viewer first paint, especially on
mobile/slow connections, which is the primary way visitors experience
this platform (section 7.3).
issue.title: Add delta encoding for replay turns array to cut replay JSON size

issue.description:
All four ACB WorkflowTemplates failed on iad-ci on 2026-08-06, twice each
(runs ~94m and ~99m apart). Observed 2026-08-06 12:35Z.

| workflow | failing node | exit |
|---|---|---|
| acb-build-dqhxq / -fv7fs | build-api, build-worker, build-enrichment, build-evolver, build-map-evolver, build-matchmaker, build-index-builder — all 7 | 1 |
| acb-enrichment-build-lp6x4 / -swt79 | docker-build | 1 |
| acb-images-build-np4cs / -s4b8n | test | 128 |
| acb-site-pages-build-q2h78 / -sfmwc | 4 retries, "No more retries left" | 128 |

## Likely root cause: the sensor is not expanding the commit SHA

Every failed run carries its `commit-sha` parameter as the **literal
unexpanded string**:

    commit-sha = {{dependencies.acb-push.body.after}}

That is the Argo Events trigger template, not a SHA. A `git checkout` of
that literal ref fails with **exit 128**, which is exactly what
acb-images-build (`test`) and acb-site-pages-build report. The exit-1
failures in acb-build/acb-enrichment are plausibly the same checkout
failure surfacing later in the build.

`acb-build.yml` declares the parameter as `sha` with the comment "Short
commit SHA, supplied by the Argo Events sensor", while the submitted
workflows pass `commit-sha`. Worth checking whether the sensor and the
template disagree on the parameter name — that would leave `sha` unset and
`commit-sha` unexpanded, matching what we see.

## Where to look

- `declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/acb-eventsensor.yml` —
  the `acb-push` dependency and its `dataTemplate`/parameter wiring
- `declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/acb-build.yml` —
  parameter named `sha`, no default
- repo: `git.ardenone.com/jedarden/ai-code-battle`

## Reproducing

Pod logs are gone (`podGC: OnPodCompletion`). To capture them, resubmit with
a `podGC: OnWorkflowCompletion` override, or stream while running.

Note: these ran while iad-ci could not schedule new pods (see the capacity
bead in declarative-config), so confirm the failures are independent of that.
issue.title: ACB CI: all four build templates failing on iad-ci; sensor passes commit-sha as an unexpanded {{...}} template (git exit 128)

issue.description:
Two features already exist independently but aren't connected:

- Win probability + critical moments (docs/plan/plan.md section 13.2,
  engine/winprob.go ComputeWinProbability): each replay stores a
  critical_moments array (turn, delta, description) for turns where win
  probability shifted >15%.
- Clip maker (web/src/pages/clip-maker.ts): lets a user pick a replay,
  scrub to a start/end turn, and export MP4/GIF in 5 social presets.
  Grepped clip-maker.ts for "critical_moment"/"criticalMoment" -- no hits,
  confirming it's not reading the field at all today.

Currently a user has to already know (or manually scrub to find) the
interesting moment in a match before they can clip it. Wire
clip-maker.ts to read the replay's critical_moments array (already fetched
as part of the replay JSON) and offer one-click "jump to critical moment
N" buttons that set the clip start/end range around that turn (e.g.
critical_moment.turn +/- ~15 turns), the same way the replay viewer's
win-probability graph already supports "click to jump" / "next critical
moment" per section 13.2.

Value: turns "watch a 5-minute replay to find the good part" into "click
the pre-flagged highlight, export it" -- directly serves the platform's
own stated shareability goal (section 13's clip-maker, embed.html,
og-tags.ts) with near-zero new backend work since the data already
exists in the replay.
issue.title: Cross-wire critical_moments into clip-maker: auto-suggest clip start/end from the win-probability critical moments

uploadReplay in cmd/acb-worker/main.go). Add two more small writes after a

cmd/acb-worker already holds (no new secrets needed) and served through

Cache-Control: max-age=10, matching the convention already used for
evolution/live.json (cmd/acb-evolver/internal/live/r2.go).

Depends on nothing blocking -- can ship independently of the
cmd/acb-index-builder compile fix, since it's a separate binary
(acb-worker) writing a separate object.

leaderboard/live-delta.json in R2 reflect it within the worker's normal
upload latency (seconds, not the ~90 min Pages deploy cycle).

issue.description:
Rename the default branch from `master` to `main` to match the convention
used by every other repo in the workspace.

No force-push is involved: this creates a new ref at the same commit, not
a history rewrite.

## Repo-side surfaces

| surface | current | how |
|---|---|---|
| Forgejo default branch | `master` | `PATCH /api/v1/repos/jedarden/ai-code-battle` `{"default_branch":"main"}` (branch must exist first) |
| GitHub mirror default | `master` (only branch) | `gh api -X PATCH repos/jedarden/ai-code-battle -f default_branch=main` — only after the push mirror has carried `main` across |
| Cloudflare Pages production branch | `master` | **Cloudflare dashboard only** — not in the repo. See `web/CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOYMENT.md` |
| local clone (ex44) | `master` | `git branch -m master main` + reset upstream |

Docs to update (historical `notes/bf-*.md` deliberately excluded — they
record what was true at the time and should not be rewritten):

- `PROGRESS.md:58,165`
- `DEPLOYMENT_STEPS.md:65`
- `web/CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOYMENT.md:14,19`
- `web/DEPLOYMENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md:77`

## Verified as non-issues (2026-08-06)

- No branch protection rules on Forgejo
- No open pull requests
- **No ArgoCD Application tracks this repo** — ArgoCD tracks
  declarative-config only, so there is no GitOps sync impact
- No clone on the lab server; ex44 is the only working copy
- `.github/workflows/*.disabled` — GH Actions stay disabled
- The Forgejo webhook fires on all pushes; branch filtering is done by the
  sensor, so the webhook itself needs no change

## Cross-repo ordering

The CI-side changes live in declarative-config and bracket this bead:

1. declarative-config **bf-637** — sensors accept both refs (before)
2. **this bead** — rename, defaults, external settings, docs
3. declarative-config **bf-2sg** — template defaults -> `main`, then drop
   `master` from the sensor filters after a soak

Cloudflare Pages is the one surface with no automation path; if its
production branch is not updated, production deploys silently become
preview deploys. Check bf-414 first — it may move Pages onto Argo
`acb-site-build`, which would remove this surface entirely.

## Do not start while ACB CI is red

Blocked on bf-1dla (sensor passes `commit-sha` as an unexpanded
`{{dependencies.acb-push.body.after}}`, exit-128 checkouts) and on
declarative-config bf-37c (iad-ci cannot schedule pods at all). Renaming
now adds a third variable to a system that cannot currently produce a
green build, so a failure afterwards could not be attributed.

Get one green ACB build first, then rename.
issue.title: Rename default branch master -> main (Forgejo, GitHub mirror, Cloudflare Pages, docs)

issue.description:
Read and analyze the focus-fire phase code in engine/turn.go to understand:
- How focus-fire targets are selected
- How damage is calculated and applied
- What conditions trigger focus-fire vs single-target combat
- The relationship between zone shrink and combat convergence

Document the current implementation with code references.

Acceptance criteria:
- Complete code walkthrough documented
- Focus-fire algorithm understood
- Edge cases identified
- Diagram of flow created if complex
issue.notes:
## Focus-Fire Combat Analysis Complete

Analyzed engine/turn.go (lines 201-290) for focus-fire implementation.

### Core Algorithm (executeCombat):
**Lines 203-223**: Target Selection
- Counts enemies within AttackRadius2 (default 12 = 3.5 tile radius) for each bot
- Uses toroidal distance via Grid.InRadius() (grid.go:114-116)
- Builds: enemyCounts[botID] = count, botsInRadius[botID] = [enemies]

**Lines 225-248**: Death Resolution (Simultaneous)
- Bot dies IF: myEnemyCount >= ANY enemy's enemyCount
- Result: If evenly matched or outnumbered by ANY enemy → death
- Only survives if strictly outnumbering ALL enemies in range
- Pre-computed counts prevent cascade effects (true simultaneous resolution)

**Lines 250-290**: Damage/Kill Tracking
- Binary alive/dead system (no HP)
- All enemies within attack radius credited as 'killers'
- Each killer awarded: gs.Config.KillScore (default 1 point)
- CombatDeaths[] tracked per player for MatchResult

### Focus-Fire vs Single-Target:
**No distinction** - same algorithm applies globally:
- Single-target scenario: 1 enemy in range → compare counts
- Focus-fire scenario: multiple enemies → death if ANY enemy has <= your count
- Emerges naturally from death condition (mutual destruction when evenly matched)

### Zone Shrink & Combat Convergence (lines 116-175):
- Zone activates at ZoneStartTurn (default turn 10)
- Center fixed at map center (set in NewGameState)
- Shrinks 1 tile per turn (ZoneShrinkInterval=1, ZoneShrinkStep=1)
- Initial radius: 90% of center-to-edge distance (setInitialZoneRadius, lines 180-199)
- Bots outside ZoneRadius killed instantly (lines 147-174)
- Minimum radius: ZoneMinRadius (1 for 3+ players, 2 for 2-player)
- Forces convergence by shrinking playable area → increases bot density → ensures contact

### Edge Cases Identified:
1. **Zero enemies**: Safe (line 234-236: if myEnemyCount == 0, continue)
2. **Self-collision**: Handled in executeMoves (lines 102-106), not combat phase
3. **Multiple killers**: All enemies in radius get kill credit (lines 262-276)
4. **Zone timing**: Zone starts BEFORE first move submitted (RunMatch activation), bots see it active
5. **Overshoot prevention**: Zone radius clamped to ZoneMinRadius (lines 132-139)
6. **Toroidal wrap**: Distance calculation accounts for map wrapping (grid.go:79-96)

### Configuration Dependencies (types.go):
- AttackRadius2: 12 (3.5 tiles) for 3+ players, 25 (5 tiles) for 2 players (lines 251, 257)
- KillScore: 1 point per kill (line 201)
- ZoneStartTurn: 10 (forces early combat vs energy farming, line 247/253)
- ZoneMinRadius: 1 for 3+ players, 2 for 2-player (lines 250, 257)

### Flow Relationship:
1. executeMoves() - bots move, collisions resolved
2. executeCombat() - focus-fire damage (simultaneous)
3. executeZone() - shrinking zone kills outsiders
4. executeCaptures() - core razing
5. executeCollection() - energy gathering
6. executeSpawns() - new bots at cores

Key insight: Zone shrink creates natural convergence by reducing play area, forcing bots into AttackRadius2 proximity of each other, guaranteeing combat before energy farming dominates.
issue.title: Analyze focus-fire phase implementation in engine/turn.go
